name: Tamuken
backstory: An independent trader in Terfila, not of any great house, who's paid tolls and delays from the crossing dispute for years no matter which side is telling the truth about it.

experience.text: Had a child with Farlo, named Farmuken.
Heard that Trezco and Forliamus now have a child, Forliazco.
Had a child with Trezco, named Tamuzco.
Heard that Forliamus and Farlo now have a child, Forliarlo.
Had a child with Forliazco, named Forliuken.
Heard that Forliazco and Farlo now have a child, Farliazco.

criterion.standard: counts a roof over the stalls above one more year of the temple eating whatever's left in the treasury
criterion.wasted_life: watching another season's coin go to arguing over old stones while the market he actually trades under stays open to the rain
criterion.origin: collision between his backstory (an independent trader who's paid the crossing's costs for years no matter who's right) and the sample's own tale: crossing_market_roof (a competing, practical use for the same limited coin)
criterion.trusts: a story that's been carried and retold and still holds together
criterion.distrusts: a record that insists on a precision no one who was actually there ever needed

previous.standard: counts staying out of a fight that costs him money either way he leans
previous.wasted_life: a life spent paying tolls and delays for a fight that isn't his, and picking a side anyway
previous.origin: collision between his backstory (pays the dispute's cost regardless of who's right) and the conflict itself

history.note: re-derived after encodings.json gained three new concrete concepts (crossing_market_roof, toll_ledger_arrears, forliamus_betrothal_offer) via /tell, at the author's explicit direction, to diversify arcs away from the epistemic-conflict default

routines.routine_actions: haggles for cart space at the market before dawn, keeps his own ledger of every toll he's paid and to whom, avoids the tavern talk about who started it

arc.premise: Tamuken wants his own toll ledger reconciled against whatever the tollhouse keeps on its side - if the arrears run his way for once, he wants the coin counted and returned, not waved off the way every dispute on this road usually is.
